plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and dense spikes of fragrant flowers. It thrives in sunny, well-drained soils and is widely grown in gardens and commercial fields for its essential oil.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer (June to August in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Mediterranean region, southern France (Provence), England, and temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years in perfumes, bathing, and medicine; the name comes from the Latin 'lavare,' meaning 'to wash.'

plants.name: Rosa gallica
plants.description: One of the oldest cultivated roses, forming a low, suckering shrub with fragrant, richly colored semi-double flowers. It is a parent of many modern garden roses and blooms abundantly in mid-June.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to midsummer (June in temperate Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Central and southern Europe and western Asia; cultivated in gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Rosa gallica 'Officinalis,' the Apothecary's Rose, was used in medieval medicine and is said to have been the emblem of the House of Lancaster.

plants.name: Leucanthemum vulgare
plants.description: A hardy perennial wildflower with classic white petals around a yellow center, growing in meadows, roadsides, and grasslands. Its flowering stems rise up to 60 cm above lobed basal leaves.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer (May to August)
plants.location: Native to Europe and temperate Asia; naturalized in North America, Australia, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: In some regions it is called the 'moon daisy' because its white petals appear to glow in the twilight of midsummer evenings.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub producing the largest flower heads of any protea, with a bowl of pink bracts surrounding a central mass of tiny flowers. It is adapted to nutrient-poor soils and fire-prone fynbos habitat.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to spring in the Southern Hemisphere, with peak bloom from about May to September
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape of South Africa; grown in Australia, California, and Hawaii
plants.funFact: King Protea is the national flower of South Africa, and its flower heads can reach up to 30 cm across.
